Note on methodology: Texas is above block-group level, and the Census's *median* household income variable (B19013) is only valid at the block-group level in this dataset — it cannot be summed or averaged across block groups to get a state median. So per the substitution rule, I computed the **mean** instead, as SUM(aggregate household income) / SUM(total households), both aggregated from all Texas block groups. This is an estimated mean, not an exact point-in-time figure, and it is not the same statistic as the commonly cited "median household income" for Texas (which tends to be lower than the mean due to income skew).
